t: This title may be cited as the “Federal Legislative Salary Act of 1966”.

fable.w: This section only provides a short title for the title of the Act. It establishes no process involving any party outside the federal government, such as a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue. There is no real tempting contrary reading; nothing in the text is on-topic.

qwen_block.w: This section is a short title citation clause. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. It merely provides the name by which the act is known.
qwen_block.s: This title may be cited as the “Federal Legislative Salary Act of 1966”.

opus.w: This section only gives the title's short name and sets up no decision-making process. Nobody inside or outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The word "Legislative" in the name does not create any participation.
opus.b: This is just a short-title clause. Someone might be tempted by the word "Legislative," but nothing here involves any process, decision, or outside party.
